newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania brewer to spend $65 mln on expansion.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania brewer to spend $65 mln on expansion.

text.p: Tanzania Breweries Ltd (TBL), the country's largest brewer, said on Thursday it planned to invest $65 million over three years and double production by the year 2000.

Annual production at the Dar es Salaam brewery would increase to 150 million litres from 75 million and production at the Mwanza plant on Lake Victoria would rise to 60 million litres from 30 million, said TBL chief executive director Danie Niemandt.

"We will double the production by about the end of next year in Mwanza. And at the same time we'll have taken Dar es Salaam from 75 to 110 (million litres) and then in 1999 to 150 (million litres)," he said.
The decision to boost production was spurred by increasing local demand for the beer and TBL was keeping an eye on opportunities for regional exports.

TBL is a joint venture between South African Breweries (SAB) local subsidiary Indol-International which holds a 45.89 percent stake against a government equity of 40.35 percent. The remainder is split between four shareholders.
The loss-making state-run brewery was privatised in 1993 under an economic reform programme started in 1986.
TBL last year added Kilimanjaro and a local version of the popular South African lager Castle to its staple production of Safari Lager.

Production is currently confined to crates of returnable 500 ml bottles retailing for around Tshs 500 per bottle, but TBL said it was likely to start producing (300-375ml) non-returnable bottles and widen its product range.
On Tuesday TBL chairman Paul Bomani said the company's market share had risen from around 30 percent in 1993 to 80 percent.

The main competitors vying for a slice of the local beer market are Belgium's Amstel, Dutch Heineken and the privately-owned Associated Breweries based in Dar es Salaam, which bottles Serengeti Lager.
